source.title: Don't be lazy: CompleteP enables compute-efficient deep transformers
source.authors: Nolan Dey; Bin Zhang; Lorenzo Noci; Mufan Li; Blake Bordelon; Shane Bergsma; Cengiz Pehlevan; Boris Hanin; Joel Hestness

record.tranche_reason: The study fits validation cross-entropy against compute and measures how loss changes across transformer shapes, but it does not reproduce the original studies’ full scaling-law or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports power-law fits against FLOPs on a compute-efficient frontier and loss comparisons across widths and depths. It does not report independent parameter-count or token-count power-law sweeps, or tests of small-run predictions on much larger runs. Hyperparameter-transfer curves, downstream evaluations at one parameter count, and model-shape results without reported loss values are not rows for other claim versions.
record.test_reason: Section 5 re-runs Kaplan's fixed-parameter width/depth (N:L) comparison at 50M, 300M and 1.5B non-embedding parameters with depth-aware parameterizations. It reports how much loss rises away from the optimal shape. It argues that Kaplan's shape conclusion was confounded by SP lacking depth control, and its results show that shape-insensitivity depends on the parameterization. The FLOP power-law fit is used as a tool: 3 points, no fit quality reported, used only for interpolation. So it does not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CompleteP (α=1) uniquely gives depth-wise HP transfer and non-lazy (complete) feature learning. They report 12–34% FLOP savings over µP, rising with depth, and a wider range of near-compute-optimal width/depth ratios (N:L≈10 within 1% at 1.5B). They also find optimal N:L grows with scale and say their FLOP fits are for interpolation only.
record.recipe_differences: This is a study of transformer parameterizations and depth/width compute efficiency, not a reproduction of the original scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported loss and compute efficiency vary with parameterization and N:L shape; the paper also notes that optimal N:L increases with model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Compute-optimal N:L grows with model size (Finding 4) and stays below ≈60 for 50M–1.5B, against Kaplan's ≈100. The optimum is similar for µP and CompleteP; α=0.5 prefers wider models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal transformer aspect ratio increases with scale and depends on the parameterization.

record.problems: The compute-frontier power-law fits use only 3 points because of budget constraints; the authors state these span a 256x FLOP range and use the fits for interpolation rather than extrapolation. Uncertainty is not reported for the validation-loss values in the scaling and shape comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No tabled downstream task scores were included: Table 2 evaluates several downstream tasks at the same approximate parameter count and does not test predictable improvement with scale or pretraining loss. Hyperparameter-transfer plots and the depth-laziness toy-network result do not measure a claim version’s loss scaling or shape sensitivity.

untested.parts: The power-law form is not tested: 3 points, no fit quality, and no parameter- or token-only sweeps.
All of it. The authors use the fits for interpolation only.
All of it. The parameter/token ratio is fixed at 20 TPP.
Only width/depth ratio in dense pre-LN transformers is varied. Other architecture details and other families are not tested.
No scaling of downstream performance with size and no fitted loss-to-downstream relation.
No comparison of exponents or allocations across fitting choices.

missing.what: µP within-1%-of-optimal range at 1.5B reaches only N:L=38.7, versus 11.8 for CompleteP. Needed as a row paired with r5.
Full loss-increase-versus-N:L curves for 7–10 shapes per size and parameterization, with the cubic-fit ≤1% ranges. These are figure-only.
Optimal N:L rises with model size (Finding 4).
Downstream average accuracy for six 1.5B models largely tracks validation loss: e.g. 2.286 gives 55.2 and 2.417 gives 50.1. This is at fixed size with no fitted relation, so it is weak evidence only.

record.verdict_notes: T5 is chosen because the paper argues that Kaplan's shape result was confounded by SP and shows that shape-insensitivity depends on the parameterization. Its CompleteP results nonetheless largely support V4. Percentages were computed from Tables 2 and 3. Raw-loss comparisons ignore small FLOP differences between shapes; the paper's own metric uses distance to the fitted FLOP curve. No SP results appear in the Section 5 tables. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests validation cross-entropy versus FLOPs on a compute-efficient frontier; does not independently test scaling with parameter count or tokens while the other quantities are not bottlenecks.
The authors say the fits are used for interpolation rather than extrapolation; no small-run to much-larger-run prediction test is reported.
Uses fixed 20 tokens per parameter for the main compute-efficient shape study; it studies width-to-depth ratios, not how optimal parameter and token counts separately grow with compute.

Tests changes in width-to-depth ratio at approximately fixed non-embedding parameter count, with other architecture details held to the study’s setup; does not test arbitrary architecture details or other model families.
Tests text pretraining only; no other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.
Reports downstream task scores for models at one parameter count, but does not test whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations across fitting choices or setups.

relationships.condition: Parameterization choice: µP and α=0.5 versus CompleteP
relationships.reason: Under µP, only N:L ≥38.7 stays within 1% at 1.5B (text, Finding 6; not in rows). Deepest shapes cost 3.2–4.3% under µP/α=0.5 versus 1.9–3.2% under CompleteP (r9, r10, r15, r16, r21, r22).

tranche.reason: Section 5 explicitly revisits the original shape conclusion, identifies depth-dependent hyperparameter detuning as a confound, and finds parameterization- and scale-dependent near-optimal shape ranges.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the January 2026 v4 revision. The 11.8 boundary comes from cubic fits to FLOP-adjusted losses, not a directly trained shape; the nearby trained shape is N:L=12.3. V4 gives no numerical definition of slightly, so the partial states and scope limits are qualitative.
